bracket.name: bracket

params.description: Length of the plate that goes against the wall, up the wall.
params.name: wall_length_mm

params.description: Length of the plate that sticks out, carrying the load.
params.name: shelf_length_mm

params.description: How wide the bracket is.
params.name: width_mm

params.description: Plate thickness. 6 mm in PETG carries a shelf; below 4 it flexes and the fixings pull through.
params.name: thickness_mm

params.description: Fillet on the inside corner. Leave unset for 1.5 x thickness, which is where the stress raiser stops mattering.
params.name: corner_r_mm

params.description: A triangular web across the corner. It carries the bending moment into the wall plate instead of the corner, and it is why a printed bracket holds.
params.name: gusset

params.description: Gusset thickness. Leave unset to match the plates.
params.name: gusset_thickness_mm

params.description: How far along each plate the gusset reaches, as a fraction.
params.name: gusset_fraction

params.description: Fixing holes in the wall plate.
params.name: wall_holes

params.description: Fixing holes in the shelf plate.
params.name: shelf_holes

params.description: Fixing hole diameter. 5.5 clears an M5; 4.5 an M4.
params.name: hole_dia_mm

params.description: Counterbore depth for a screw head to sit flush. 0 for none. The bore is on the OUTSIDE face, so it prints as a plain step.
params.name: counterbore_mm

params.description: Distance from a hole centre to the plate edge. Leave unset for 1.4 x the hole diameter, below which the material tears out.
params.name: edge_margin_mm

print_notes: Orientation: standing on the back edge of the wall plate. DO NOT ROTATE - printed flat this is about a third as strong.
No supports needed in that orientation.
PETG or ABS. PLA creeps under a sustained load and the shelf droops.
4 walls and 40% infill. On a bracket the walls carry the load, so wall count matters far more than infill density.
Layer 0.2 mm. Finer does not make it stronger.
bracket.summary: An L of two plates with a gusset across the corner and fixing holes. Prints standing on its back edge so the layers run across the load.

cable_box.name: cable_box

params.description: The pattern on the outside. plain is flat faces, which is most of why a downloaded model looks better than a generated one. ribs and flutes are vertical grooves; facets cut flats round a cylinder; hex and knurl are shallow pockets; waves are horizontal rings.
params.name: finish

params.description: Centre to centre of the pattern.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: How wide each cut, or each cell, is.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How far into the wall. Left out, whichever is smaller of 0.7 mm and a third of the wall - a decoration that takes more than a third of the wall is a weakness, and one that reaches the cavity is a hole. Given explicitly it is checked, not clamped.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Outside, end to end. A four-way strip is about 230 mm long, a six-way about 320 - measure the strip, this is the number that decides whether it goes in.
params.name: width_mm

params.description: Outside, front to back. A strip is 45-55 mm wide; the rest is cable.
params.name: depth_mm

params.description: Outside, floor to the top of the lid. Tall enough for the strip plus the plugs standing in it - the plugs are the tall part.
params.name: height_mm

params.description: It holds air, not load. 2.4 mm is six passes of a 0.4 nozzle - stiff enough to pick up full, and a third of the plastic of a structural wall.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: Across the slot at each end. Sized for a moulded PLUG to pass, not the cable - a UK plug is 50 mm across, a European one 38.
params.name: cable_slot_w_mm

params.description: Up from the floor. A plug body is 25-30 mm deep.
params.name: cable_slot_h_mm

params.description: Slots in the sides and the lid. ON by default and worth leaving on: a sealed box around a power strip and three chargers is the one mistake in this design that matters.
params.name: vents

params.description: Width of each vent slot.
params.name: vent_slot_mm

params.description: Gap between the lid's rebate and the box. Left out, it is the material's own measured clearance - the figure harvested from parts that actually printed and fitted.
params.name: lid_clearance_mm

params.description: How far the lid's lip drops inside the box to locate it.
params.name: lid_lip_mm

params.description: How far the box stands off the desk. The cable slots are at floor level, so without feet the cables are pinched under it. 0 turns them off.
params.name: feet_mm

params.description: Outline rounding. Left out, 2 x the wall.
params.name: corner_r_mm

cable_box.summary: A lidded box for a power strip: a plug-sized slot at each end at floor level, vent slots through the sides and lid, feet to keep the cables off the desk, and a lid that locates on a lip with the material's own clearance.

clip.name: clip

params.description: Across the thing being gripped. A mains cable is 6-8 mm, a broom handle 22-25, a 15 mm pipe is 15. This is the number everything else is worked out from.
params.name: bore_mm

params.description: Along the thing. Longer grips better and needs more push.
params.name: length_mm

params.description: The arms, which ARE the spring. Thick enough to hold, thin enough to open - about 45% of the bore radius. This is the one number that decides whether the clip works, and a wall wrong for the bore is refused with the figure it should be.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: How wide the mouth is as a fraction of the bore. Below 1 it snaps over and holds; at 1 it is a cradle and the thing falls out. 0.72 grips a cable firmly.
params.name: mouth_fraction

params.description: Material behind the bore, which is what it is fixed through.
params.name: back_mm

params.description: A screw hole through the back. Left out, there is none and the clip is glued or taped - which is what most cable clips are.
params.name: screw_dia_mm

clip.summary: A C that springs over something round and holds it: the mouth is narrower than the bore, flared so it guides in, and the arm thickness is worked out from the bore because the arms are the spring. Prints lying down so the layers run around the C.

container.name: container

params.description: The pattern on the outside. plain is flat faces, which is most of why a downloaded model looks better than a generated one. ribs and flutes are vertical grooves; facets cut flats round a cylinder; hex and knurl are shallow pockets; waves are horizontal rings.
params.name: finish

params.description: Centre to centre of the pattern.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: How wide each cut, or each cell, is.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How far into the wall. Left out, whichever is smaller of 0.7 mm and a third of the wall - a decoration that takes more than a third of the wall is a weakness, and one that reaches the cavity is a hole. Given explicitly it is checked, not clamped.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Square holds more in a drawer and stacks; round is stronger for the same wall and has no corners to clean out.
params.name: shape

params.description: Outside, left to right, AT THE RIM - the widest point. Square bodies only. The rim is the number that decides whether it goes in the drawer.
params.name: width_mm

params.description: Outside, front to back, at the rim. Square bodies only.
params.name: depth_mm

params.description: Outside across the rim. Round bodies only.
params.name: diameter_mm

params.description: Outside, floor to rim.
params.name: height_mm

params.description: How far the walls lean in going down. 0 is a straight tub. 6-10 degrees makes them nest inside one another when empty, which is what a stack of takeaway tubs is doing.
params.name: taper_deg

params.description: The side wall. 2.4 is two perimeters of a 0.6 nozzle.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: The floor. Left out, 1.4 x the wall - the floor is what gets set down on a table and what the contents press on.
params.name: floor_mm

params.description: Corner rounding on a square body. Left out, 3 x the wall.
params.name: corner_r_mm

params.description: Compartments left to right. More than one makes it a lunch box rather than a tub. Square bodies only.
params.name: columns

params.description: Compartments front to back.
params.name: rows

params.description: open: a tub, no lid. lid: a lid that drops into the mouth on a skirt. clip: the same lid with snap tabs that click over a groove - it stays shut upside down. magnet: held by magnets in the rim, which opens with one finger. hinge: knuckles at the back and a printed pin, so the lid cannot be put down and lost.
params.name: closure

params.description: How far the lid's skirt reaches down inside. Left out, 18% of the height and never under 4 mm - a short skirt lets the lid rock and lift off.
params.name: lid_skirt_mm

params.description: The air between lid and body. Left out, the MATERIAL'S OWN measured clearance from config - a figure harvested from test prints, not chosen here.
params.name: lid_clearance_mm

params.description: Magnet diameter. 6 x 3 discs are the common size.
params.name: magnet_dia_mm

params.description: Magnet thickness.
params.name: magnet_thick_mm

params.description: How many pairs. Four is a lid that will not twist off.
params.name: magnet_count

params.description: Snap tabs around the skirt. Two opposite each other is a lid you can pop with a thumb; four needs two hands.
params.name: snap_tab_count

params.description: How far the snap bead stands proud. Left out, 35% of the skirt thickness - see SNAP_BEAD_FRACTION, which shows the deflection that figure came from. This is an ASSUMPTION and is reported.
params.name: snap_bead_mm

params.description: Hinge pin. Printed as a third body, or use a 3 mm rod.
params.name: pin_dia_mm

params.description: A groove in the underside that sits over the rim - or over the lid's raised ring - of the one below, so a stack does not slide.
params.name: stackable

container.summary: A box or tub - square or round, straight or tapered, in one piece or divided into compartments - with a lid that drops on, clips shut on snap tabs, holds with magnets or swings on a pinned hinge. The outside can carry ribs, flutes, facets, a honeycomb, a knurl or horizontal waves rather than being four flat faces.

enclosure.name: enclosure

params.description: X, outside width.
params.name: width_mm

params.description: Y, outside depth.
params.name: depth_mm

params.description: Z, outside height of the box, not counting the roof.
params.name: height_mm

params.description: Wall thickness. 3 mm is sound for a birdhouse in PETG.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: Floor thickness. Leave unset to match the wall.
params.name: floor_mm

params.description: Vertical corner radius on the outside.
params.name: corner_r_mm

params.description: Entrance hole diameter. 32 mm suits a starling, 28 a great tit, 25 a blue tit. Set 0 for no entrance - a plain box.
params.name: entrance_dia_mm

params.description: Height of the entrance centre above the floor. Leave unset to put it in the upper third, which keeps chicks away from a reaching cat.
params.name: entrance_height_mm

params.description: Which wall the entrance goes in: front, back, left or right.
params.name: entrance_face

params.description: A raised collar around the entrance, thickening the wall so a cat or a squirrel cannot reach through to the nest. 18 to 25 mm is usual. 0 for none.
params.name: predator_guard_mm

params.description: Extend the back wall this far above and below the box, giving a flat plate to screw to a tree or a post. 0 for none.
params.name: back_plate_mm

params.description: Include a roof. Printed as a separate piece.
params.name: roof

params.description: How far the roof stands proud on every side, to shed rain clear of the entrance.
params.name: roof_overhang_mm

params.description: Roof slab thickness.
params.name: roof_thick_mm

params.description: Roof slope. Printed FLAT and set on at an angle, so the slope costs no support. 0 gives a flat roof.
params.name: roof_pitch_deg

params.description: Roof shape. 'gable' is the triangular two-sided roof people picture when they say birdhouse: two panels meeting at a ridge along the width. 'mono' is a single panel leaning one way. 'flat' is a lid. All three print flat and are set on afterwards, so none of them costs support.
params.name: roof_style

params.description: Depth of the lip under the roof that drops into the cavity and locates the lid. For FLAT lids. A lip cannot enter a rectangular hole while the lid is tilted, so a pitched roof wants 0 and glue.
params.name: roof_lip_mm

params.description: Gap between the lip and the box, so the roof lifts off.
params.name: roof_clearance_mm

params.description: Exterior relief. plain is flat. board cuts horizontal shiplap grooves for a weatherboard look and slat cuts vertical reveals for a modern slatted panel look - both of those belong to this box. ribs, flutes, facets, hex, knurl and waves are the catalogue's shared patterns and mean the same here as on anything else.
params.name: finish

params.description: Spacing between grooves, centre to centre.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: Width of each groove. Must be at least two nozzle widths to resolve.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How deep the grooves cut into the wall.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Drainage holes in the floor. A birdhouse without them rots.
params.name: drain_holes

params.description: Drainage hole diameter.
params.name: drain_dia_mm

params.description: Ventilation slots near the top of each side wall.
params.name: vent_slots

params.description: Two screw holes through the back wall for mounting.
params.name: mount_holes

params.description: Mounting hole diameter.
params.name: mount_dia_mm

print_notes: Two pieces: the box upright, the roof flat beside it. Do not rotate.
No supports. The cavity opens upward and the entrance is a horizontal bore.
Layer height 0.2 to 0.28 mm. This is a big part and detail is not the point.
PETG or ASA outdoors. PLA goes brittle in UV within a season.
3 walls and 15% infill is plenty - the walls carry it, not the infill.
Glue the roof on at the stated pitch, or leave it loose to clean the box out.
No perch, deliberately: nest-box birds do not need one and it gives a predator somewhere to stand.
enclosure.summary: RECTANGULAR. For anything round use `vessel`. A hollow box: walls, a floor, an optional opening in one wall, an optional lift-off roof or lid, drainage, ventilation, a predator guard and a mounting plate. Everything optional is off by setting it to zero, so a plain open-topped box is this template with the extras turned off.

gridfinity.name: gridfinity

params.description: The pattern on the outside. plain is flat faces, which is most of why a downloaded model looks better than a generated one. ribs and flutes are vertical grooves; facets cut flats round a cylinder; hex and knurl are shallow pockets; waves are horizontal rings.
params.name: finish

params.description: Centre to centre of the pattern.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: How wide each cut, or each cell, is.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How far into the wall. Left out, whichever is smaller of 0.7 mm and a third of the wall - a decoration that takes more than a third of the wall is a weakness, and one that reaches the cavity is a hole. Given explicitly it is checked, not clamped.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Grid cells left to right. Each is 42 mm.
params.name: units_x

params.description: Grid cells front to back. Each is 42 mm.
params.name: units_y

params.description: Height units of 7 mm. A 3U bin stands 21 mm and holds about 14 mm - the foot takes the first unit, which is why 1U is not offered as a bin.
params.name: units_z

params.description: The shell. Nothing structural happens to a bin wall; 1.2 mm is three passes of a 0.4 nozzle and is what the common bins use.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: Above the foot, under the contents.
params.name: floor_mm

params.description: Compartments across. 1 is a plain bin.
params.name: divisions_x

params.description: Compartments front to back.
params.name: divisions_y

params.description: 6 x 2 mm magnet pockets in the underside, one per grid cell, so the bin stays put in a drawer that gets pulled. Off by default: they need magnets, and a pocket with nothing in it is a hole.
params.name: magnets

params.description: A sweep up the front wall of each compartment so small parts can be swept out with a thumb. The detail that makes a bin usable one-handed.
params.name: scoop

params.description: Build the BASEPLATE for this footprint instead of the bin - the grid of pockets the bins drop into.
params.name: baseplate

gridfinity.summary: A Gridfinity bin or baseplate built to the published standard: 42 mm grid, 41.5 mm footprint, 7 mm height units and the 0.8/1.8/2.15 foot, so it drops into anybody else's baseplate.

hook.name: hook

params.description: Across the backplate.
params.name: plate_width_mm

params.description: Up the wall. Tall enough for two screws far enough apart that the hook cannot rotate about a single one.
params.name: plate_height_mm

params.description: Thickness of the backplate. This is what the screw pulls against, so below 3 mm the head sinks into it.
params.name: plate_thick_mm

params.description: How far the arm stands out from the wall. The moment at the root is load x this, so a long reach needs a thicker arm.
params.name: reach_mm

params.description: The arm's section. 9 mm in PETG holds a coat; a bag needs more. This is the number that decides whether it snaps.
params.name: arm_thick_mm

params.description: How far the tip turns up. Left out, it is 60% of the opening - enough to stop things lifting off, not so much that they will not go on. 0 makes it a peg rather than a hook.
params.name: tip_rise_mm

params.description: The gap between the tip and the wall - what has to pass through to get onto the hook. A coat loop is 5-10 mm, a bag strap 30-40.
params.name: opening_mm

params.description: Clearance hole for the screw shank.
params.name: screw_dia_mm

params.description: Two by default: one screw is a hinge, and a hook on a hinge swings sideways under load.
params.name: screw_count

params.description: Cone the hole so a countersunk head sits flush.
params.name: countersink

params.description: Fillet where the arm meets the plate. Left out, it is 0.8 x the arm thickness - this is where a printed hook cracks.
params.name: root_fillet_mm

hook.summary: A backplate and an arm that turns up at the tip, filleted at the root and screwed through countersunk holes above the arm. Prints standing on its back so the layers run across the load.

keyring_device.name: keyring_device

params.description: Overall body width across the trim caps. At 30 mm the glass side bezel lands on exactly one extrusion width; below 26 mm drop the screen detail entirely.
params.name: body_width_mm

params.description: Single constant thickness of the whole part.
params.name: depth_mm

params.description: Thinnest handle section that survives a keychain. Below 2.4 it snaps.
params.name: min_handle_mm

params.description: Thinnest engraved or embossed line worth cutting.
params.name: min_stroke_mm

params.description: How far the boss must reach past the handle on each side.
params.name: boss_margin_mm

params.description: Module pocket depth, i.e. the bezel step. Deliberately deeper than true scale: a scale-correct 0.44 mm recess is geometrically right and visually dead, with too little depth to catch a shadow.
params.name: recess_mm

params.description: Additional depth of the glass area inside the bezel.
params.name: glass_mm

params.description: Camera dot depth.
params.name: cam_mm

params.description: Attempted and reverted if OCC produces an invalid solid, which it does on this silhouette. Set to 0 to stop trying. For elephant foot use your slicer's first-layer compensation instead - that is the correct fix and costs no geometry.
params.name: front_chamfer_mm

params.description: As above, back face.
params.name: back_chamfer_mm

params.description: Engrave the traced wordmark. OFF by default because it requires logo_json, a file path that has to come from somewhere - a measured baseline showed this default costing an attempt on every keyring request that did not mention the logo. Set it true and point logo_json at the output of `whittle measure trace`.
params.name: logo_on

params.description: Path to traced logo outlines from `whittle measure trace`. Relative paths resolve against the spec file. Required when logo_on.
params.name: logo_json

params.description: Logo width as a fraction of the fabric waist width.
params.name: logo_width_fraction

params.description: Engraving depth.
params.name: logo_depth_mm

params.description: Grow the logo until its thinnest stroke is printable.
params.name: logo_autoscale

params.description: Engrave the screen UI as raised cards.
params.name: ui_on

params.description: How far the cards stand above the glass floor.
params.name: ui_raise_mm

params.description: Shrink every element slightly to keep the gaps printable.
params.name: ui_shrink_mm

print_notes: Orientation: flat, back face on the bed. DO NOT ROTATE.
Layer height 0.12 mm - the face detail is in Z, that is the whole point.
PETG. A PLA keyring at this section will snap at the handle.
4 walls, 100% infill. It is 6.5 cm3; solid costs nothing and a hollow keyring crushes.
No supports. Ironing on the top surface only, if your slicer has it.
keyring_device.summary: One-piece keyring: constant-depth extrusion, fused handle, engraved face detail.

louvre_vent.name: louvre_vent

params.description: X, outside width of the body.
params.name: frame_w_mm

params.description: Y, body depth, the insertion direction.
params.name: frame_d_mm

params.description: Z, outside height and print height.
params.name: frame_h_mm

params.description: Rail thickness top and bottom.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: Vertical corner radius on the body.
params.name: bezel_r_mm

params.description: Flange thickness in Y.
params.name: flange_t_mm

params.description: How far the flange stands proud, all round.

params.description: Screw clearance hole. 3.4 is M3 clearance.

params.description: Advisory: cut your hole this much over body size.

params.description: Number of louvre blades. Leave unset to derive from the aperture width, keeping roughly the reference 17 mm pitch and never exceeding what the crank linkage can fit.

params.description: Blade thickness in X.
params.name: blade_thick_mm

params.description: As printed. 0 = straight through.
params.name: blade_angle_deg

params.description: Mechanism travel limit. Past ~40 the bar fouls the pivot pins.

params.description: Rounding on the blade edges.

params.description: Radial clearance, pin to socket.

PETG or ABS. PLA creeps and the blades go slack.

louvre_vent.summary: Print-in-place adjustable louvre vent with a parallel-crank linkage.

stand.name: stand

params.description: How thick the thing is, INCLUDING its case. A bare phone is 7-9 mm and a cased one 10-13 mm; 11 is a cased phone. Measure yours if it matters - this is the number the slot is cut from.
params.name: device_thickness_mm

params.description: How wide the thing is across the face that rests. A phone is 70-80 mm, a small tablet about 170. The stand is made wider than this so the device is not balanced on the edges.
params.name: device_width_mm

params.description: Degrees from the bench, measured to the resting face. 65 is a desk viewing angle; 50 is closer to a typing angle; above 80 it is nearly upright and it topples. This is the single number that decides whether the stand is usable.
params.name: lean_deg

params.description: Front to back. Left out, it is worked out from the lean and the backrest height so the stand cannot tip backwards.
params.name: base_depth_mm

params.description: How far up the back the device is supported, along the lean. About half the device's height is plenty; more is material.
params.name: back_height_mm

params.description: Thickness of the shell. 3 mm is stiff enough in PETG for a phone; below 2 it flexes when the screen is pressed.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: How far the front lip stands up. Left out, it is 40% of the device thickness - enough to hold it and not so much that it covers the screen.
params.name: lip_height_mm

params.description: Cut a channel through the bottom of the slot so a charging cable reaches the socket. Without it the stand can only be used with the device unplugged, which is the opposite of what a desk stand is for.
params.name: cable_slot

params.description: Across the cable channel. A USB-C plug moulding is 10-12 mm.
params.name: cable_width_mm

params.description: Rounding on the outline. Left out, it is 1.5 x the wall.
params.name: corner_r_mm

stand.summary: A stand something leans back against: a slot sized to the device with a lip so it cannot slide out, a backrest at a readable angle, a cable channel through the front, and a hollow base so it is not a brick.

tray.name: tray

params.description: The pattern on the outside. plain is flat faces, which is most of why a downloaded model looks better than a generated one. ribs and flutes are vertical grooves; facets cut flats round a cylinder; hex and knurl are shallow pockets; waves are horizontal rings.

params.description: Centre to centre of the pattern.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: How wide each cut, or each cell, is.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How far into the wall. Left out, whichever is smaller of 0.7 mm and a third of the wall - a decoration that takes more than a third of the wall is a weakness, and one that reaches the cavity is a hole. Given explicitly it is checked, not clamped.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Outside, left to right. Measure the drawer - this is the number that decides whether it goes in.
params.name: width_mm

params.description: Outside, front to back.
params.name: depth_mm

params.description: Outside, floor to rim. Tall enough that things do not fall out, low enough to reach into.
params.name: height_mm

params.description: Compartments left to right. 1 makes it a plain tray.
params.name: columns

params.description: Compartments front to back.

params.description: The walls between compartments. Left out, 0.8 x the outer wall - they carry nothing and this is where the plastic is saved.
params.name: divider_mm

params.description: The floor. Left out, 0.8 x the outer wall: the contents rest on the drawer through it, so it is not a structural member.
params.name: floor_mm

params.description: A scoop in the front wall of each compartment. Without it you cannot get a small part out without tipping the tray - the detail that decides whether it stays in the drawer.
params.name: finger_scoop

params.description: Outline rounding. Left out, 2 x the outer wall.
params.name: corner_r_mm

tray.summary: A shallow open tray divided into a grid of compartments, with a finger scoop in the front of each, thin dividers and a thin floor. The outside can carry ribs, a honeycomb, a knurl or horizontal waves. Prints open side up with no support.

vessel.name: vessel

params.description: The pattern on the outside. plain is flat faces, which is most of why a downloaded model looks better than a generated one. ribs and flutes are vertical grooves; facets cut flats round a cylinder; hex and knurl are shallow pockets; waves are horizontal rings.
params.name: finish

params.description: Centre to centre of the pattern.
params.name: finish_pitch_mm

params.description: How wide each cut, or each cell, is.
params.name: finish_groove_mm

params.description: How far into the wall. Left out, whichever is smaller of 0.7 mm and a third of the wall - a decoration that takes more than a third of the wall is a weakness, and one that reaches the cavity is a hole. Given explicitly it is checked, not clamped.
params.name: finish_depth_mm

params.description: Diameter at the widest point of the body.
params.name: outer_dia_mm

params.description: Overall height including the foot.
params.name: height_mm

params.description: Wall thickness.
params.name: wall_mm

params.description: Thickness of the base. Defaults to a little over the wall.
params.name: floor_mm

params.description: straight is a plain cone. flared opens out towards the rim like a bowl. belly bulges in the middle and draws back in like a vase. cylinder is a straight-sided pot. custom takes the silhouette from profile_points, which is how a shape MEASURED off a mesh becomes an editable part.
params.name: profile

params.description: The silhouette as (radius_mm, height_mm) pairs from the base up. Only used when profile is custom. This is what a generated mesh turns into: measured off the surface, then editable like any other number.
params.name: profile_points

params.description: Diameter at the rim. Derived from the profile if left out.
params.name: rim_dia_mm

params.description: Diameter where it meets the foot. Derived if left out.
params.name: base_dia_mm

params.description: Height of a narrower foot ring under the body. 0 for none.
params.name: foot_mm

params.description: Foot diameter. Derived if left out.
params.name: foot_dia_mm

params.description: Rounding on the rim edge, so it is not a knife edge.
params.name: rim_round_mm

params.description: Holes through the base. A plant pot needs them, a bowl does not.
params.name: drain_holes

params.description: Diameter of each drainage hole.
params.name: drain_dia_mm

params.description: solid is a plain wall. cells cuts a Voronoi web through it, leaving a strut between every pair of holes.
params.name: pattern

params.description: How many cells around and up the wall. More means finer.
params.name: cell_count

params.description: Width of the web between two holes. This is the part that carries the load.
params.name: strut_mm

params.description: Which arrangement of cells. Change it for a different pattern of the same character. The same seed always gives the same bowl.
params.name: cell_seed

params.description: Solid band left under the rim. The rim is what holds the whole thing round.
params.name: rim_band_mm

params.description: Solid band left above the floor, so the base is not perforated.
params.name: base_band_mm

print_notes: Orientation: standing upright, exactly as modelled. The cavity opens upward, so there is nothing to support.
No supports. If the profile needed them the spec would have been refused - the wall lean is checked against 45 degrees.
Vase mode / spiralised outer contour suits this well if the wall is a single extrusion wide and there are no drainage holes.
PETG for anything that holds water. PLA is fine dry and will soften in a hot car or a dishwasher.
3 walls minimum. On a thin turned wall the walls ARE the part.
vessel.summary: A ROUND vessel turned about its axis - bowl, dish, plant pot, cup or vase. Open at the top, with a real wall, a floor and an optional foot. Use this whenever the thing is round. The enclosure template is rectangular and will make a square box out of a bowl.
